# Final requirements and regression-coverage review

Reviewer identity: `final_coverage`. Independent, read-only requirements/coverage lens. Inputs were the mechanically assembled lower/upper criteria, request, plan and diffs; the lower-r2 mechanical delta; and pinned code, contracts and Git objects. No worker conclusions or other reviewer verdicts were used.

## Verdicts

- **Lower `5a9f044f84fbcc21597f7bf44466cab9b3694b42`: could not break it; pass within this lens.** This includes scoped revalidation of the Unicode delta above reviewed lower `e126316ce6fa724b19353501a817ab89a6f08af3`.
- **Upper `3d951d8fd5cf1d06a6e73e456fe15026aa66fb9c`: changes requested for the inherited Unicode defect below.** Its upper-specific source/successor regressions pass, but this pin still carries the old lower predicate. No other correctness gap found. The reviewed lower-r2 repair has not yet been incorporated into this pinned upper.
- **Core fit: pass; reviewer `final_coverage`.** Queue integrity, source evidence and successor obligations use repository-local Markdown/Git and Python standard-library code. Their purpose survives agent, provider and adopted-repository substitution. The repair adds no user-global or provider-specific dependency. Core fit does not override the upper correctness finding.

## Finding: upper still permits newer format controls on Python 3.9

`automation/markdown_semantics.py:461` in upper `3d951d8` uses the interpreter's `unicodedata.category(...) == "Cf"` to decide which raw bytes must remain protected. Python 3.9.6 uses Unicode 13, so it does not classify the tested Arabic/Egyptian controls assigned later. These bytes, including encoded spellings, can leave the frozen skeleton in retry diagnosis or lifecycle metadata on that supported interpreter.

I executed the two lower-r2 regression methods against the **native upper runtime and helpers**, adding only the test methods in memory: **2/2 methods failed, 24 failing subcases, 0 errors, 0 skips** on Python 3.9.6. Thus this is an inherited code defect at the exact upper pin, not a missing publication/CI result. Incorporate the lower-r2 predicate repair and revalidate the combined upper candidate. The parent is already preparing that mechanical integration; this report does not assume it happened.

## Preservation and runner evidence

All six expected ancestry checks passed: current main and original PR88 precede lower; current main, original PR88, original PR89 and lower precede upper. Lower-r2 additionally retains reviewed lower as an ancestor. Every one of the **117 current-main history entries** has the same mode/object/path in both original review candidates. Original PR88 contributes 99 history entries and PR89 100; all original historical files remain exact except `history/AGENTS.md`, which takes the current-main contract. No current-main hook, review-receipt module, core/action gate or principle differs in lower-r2.

An AST audit found **0 removed original PR88 queue test methods out of 507**, and **0 removed original PR89 methods out of 512**. Five retained methods changed: a comment correction, additional lifecycle/fold checks, the explicit diagnosis exception in the byte-accounting corpus assertion, and moving the budget assertion to its canonical template README. I found no useful behavior discarded by those changes.

The actual runner discovers **536 lower / 565 upper** queue methods, including all **29 lower / 24 upper** recovery additions selected here. Lower-r2 discovers **538**, including both Unicode additions. For each layer, all five checked input mappings—reconciler, shared Markdown semantics, queue test file, review template and template README—select the queue tests through the existing runner ownership rules.

## Executed checks and controls

Default focused runs used Python **3.14.6**, Git **2.55.0**, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`. Additional interpreter runs explicitly used `/usr/bin/python3` (**3.9.6**) and `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`. Candidate repositories, indexes and configuration were not mutated. Test fixture Git writes were temporary; later scripts explicitly place fixtures beneath `/private/tmp/final-coverage-*`. The first focused candidate runs used the test helper's default temporary directory and completed/cleaned normally.

| Check | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Lower recovery additions at e126316 | 29/29 methods pass; 389 subcases; 0 failures/errors/skips |
| Upper recovery additions at 3d951d8 | 24/24 methods pass; 142 subcases; 0 failures/errors/skips |
| Original PR88/89 reconciler-body controls | Lower 19/29 and upper 20/24 methods red; 144 and 119 failing subcases; 0 errors/skips |
| Controls for methods that already passed original bodies | Lower 10/10 and upper 4/4 methods red; 144 and 7 failing subcases; 0 errors/skips |
| Lower-r2 Unicode additions, each Python | 2/2 methods pass; 28 subcases; 0 failures/errors/skips |
| Exact old Unicode predicate rollback on Python 3.9 | 2/2 methods red; 24/28 subcases red; 0 errors/skips |
| Same Unicode methods on native upper3d runtime, Python 3.9 | 2/2 methods red; 24 failing subcases; 0 errors/skips |
| Independent complete generated retry lifecycle | File → claim → diagnose → fix/delete passes, including committed range; deletion while the named finding remains is refused |
| Existing complete manual retry lifecycle | 1/1 test passes; 0 failures/errors/skips |

Together the original-body and targeted fault controls make **all 53/53 pre-r2 new recovery methods fail under at least one relevant fault**, plus both r2 methods under the old Python-3.9 predicate. The original-body controls intentionally retain candidate shared modules and templates; they are localized rollback controls, not claims of executing pristine historical trees. The remaining controls remove raw-byte protection, freeze all mutable values, omit review-target evidence, ignore source selectors, remove the unanswerable outcome, or discard concrete response bytes. None forces a test assertion directly. Per-method fault labels and results are retained in the JSON files below.

The Unicode pin was also compared exhaustively with the local Python-3.14 Unicode-16 database: **170/170 Cf codepoints match**, with no missing or extra points. Python3.9 exposes 161 of them; the nine newer assignments are the reason a pinned table is needed.

## Exact commands and retained evidence

All commands ran with working directory `/private/tmp`; scripts contain the exact selected methods, helper calls, controls and Git commands.

```sh
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-audit.py /private/tmp/agentfold-final-review-upper
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-controls.py lower candidate > /private/tmp/final-coverage-lower-candidate.log
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-controls.py upper candidate > /private/tmp/final-coverage-upper-candidate.log
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-controls.py lower original-runtime > /private/tmp/final-coverage-lower-original-runtime.log
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-controls.py upper original-runtime > /private/tmp/final-coverage-upper-original-runtime.log
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-remaining-controls.py lower > /private/tmp/final-coverage-remaining-lower.log
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-remaining-controls.py upper > /private/tmp/final-coverage-remaining-upper.log
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null /usr/bin/python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-unicode.py > /private/tmp/final-coverage-unicode-py39-candidate.log
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null /usr/bin/python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-unicode.py rollback > /private/tmp/final-coverage-unicode-py39-control.log
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 /private/tmp/final-coverage-unicode.py > /private/tmp/final-coverage-unicode-py314-candidate.log
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null /usr/bin/python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-upper-unicode.py > /private/tmp/final-coverage-upper-unicode.log
env PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null python3 /private/tmp/final-coverage-generated-lifecycle.py > /private/tmp/final-coverage-generated-lifecycle.log
```

Machine-readable results: `/private/tmp/final-coverage-audit.json`, `/private/tmp/final-coverage-{lower,upper}-{candidate,original-runtime}.json`, and `/private/tmp/final-coverage-remaining-{lower,upper}.json`. The runner-delta and protected-surface audit also executed an inline Python script calling `discovered_test_names`, `git diff --name-only main..lower-r2` on each named protected surface, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor e126316..5a9f044`; its observed results are stated above.

## Limits

This is focused verification, not a duplicated full-suite or full publication review. The parent owns both-interpreter full suites, actual-base historical admission ranges, full Git-bearing corpus runs, hosted CI, mergeability, projections and original-owner index/probe/ref preservation. I did not access the original owner's working tree/index or assert that a clean review clone proves it unchanged. Those publication and preservation gates remain necessary; their pending status is not an additional code finding. No combined upper revision newer than 3d951d8 was reviewed here.
